Chapter 10. Leaving Darfur—What Remains.
There comes a moment when you know it’s time to move on. For some, leaving happens quickly—maybe it’s because of a sudden security threat, or just the simple fact that a contract has ended. For others, it’s a long-anticipated goodbye. And honestly, it’s never just one emotion. The place that once felt so unfamiliar slowly becomes a part of you. The people you barely knew at first? Now, they’re friends you can’t imagine saying goodbye to.
Packing your bags is strangely quiet. You find yourself walking around, saying those last goodbyes, promising you’ll stay in touch, swapping small gifts as a way of saying thank you. That compound, which used to feel uncertain or even intimidating, is now filled with memories—laughter echoing down hallways, moments of fear, and flashes of hope.
Then, as the plane takes off and you look down at Darfur fading into the distance, you realize something. The chapter doesn’t really close when you leave. The lessons you learned, the friendships you made, the stories you heard—they all stay with you. They change the way you look at the world, and maybe even the way you see yourself.
But for those who remain, life goes on. The challenges are still there—just as tough as before. Yet, so is the determination to keep going. The future? It’s uncertain, sure. But hope is stubborn. You’ll find it in the resilience of the communities, in those quiet moments when someone helps a neighbor, in the belief that, yes, change is possible.
So, leaving Darfur isn’t really an ending. It’s more like the start of something new. It’s a reminder to remember—to bear witness to what you’ve seen, and to act with compassion, no matter where life takes you next.
